rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a reader who cannot resolve a pronoun/demonstrative/noun mid-deck loses the thread. Checked the two diff sites plus a full sequential pass. (a) chunk 3 line 20 'The agent is an optimizer' (swapped from 'The LLM'): 'the agent' is not a forward reference — it is FIRST used in this very file at chunk 1 line 9 ('ask your agent to walk you through...') and reused at chunk 1 line 10, chunk 3 line 22, chunk 4 line 26 — established well before chunk 3 under the sequential read, so the swap trades one already-resolved noun for another already-resolved noun. Not a violation. (b) chunk 6 line 45 (new bitter-lesson bullet): 'the next model' (x2) is a self-contained forward-looking phrase needing no antecedent (parallel to 'the next release'); 'it' in 'what it needs' binds to 'the next model' in the same sentence; 'your gates and workflow, yours or the agent's' binds to 'gate'/'agent', both established since chunk 0/1. (c) chunk 0 line 3 'the re-send'/'the verifier you built': confirmed via `grep -n '^\[' curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/learn-from-the-test.md` that this lecture is included directly after `exercises/diagnose-and-resend.md` (via `what-packaging-is.md`) — module-arc-beats-in-openers/closers carve-out applies, the referent is the student's just-finished exercise, not a missing slide. Harm absent throughout.

Harm: a slide pointing at another file by position strands the reader who starts the deck elsewhere. `sed -n '1,46p' curriculum/lectures/the-gate-is-a-claim.md | grep -niE 'the opening lecture|earlier module|previous module|last module|the module before|as we (saw|said) (earlier|before)'` -> exit 1, zero hits. Also `grep -nE '\bM[0-9]\b'` over the body -> exit 1, zero hits — no cross-module position refs anywhere in body. Harm absent.

Harm: a slide that says nothing standalone. Line closest to the concern is chunk 0's lede (title slide, only 2 sentences after the H1) — but it carries a full self-sufficient thesis ('A passing result is only as trustworthy as the check that produced it. The check itself needs verification.'), not a wait-state or context-dependent fragment, so it stays inside. All other chunks carry 2-5 substantive bullets each (see chunk_map word/bullet counts below). Harm absent everywhere.

Harm: a header the chunk's own content contradicts. Line closest to violating is chunk 6 line 45, the new bitter-lesson bullet, which shifts topic from the reach/calibration mechanics of bullets 1-4 to model-obsolescence — it stays inside 'The delegation frontier' because it extends bullet 4's own claim ('The frontier moves outward only as fast as the gates behind it', line 44) one step further: the gates that define today's frontier are themselves time-limited, so the frontier's motion is doubly qualified, not a new topic. Every other chunk's header (Gates decay/One session is a sample/etc.) is a direct label of its own bullets. Harm absent.

Harm: cadence tics that read as machine-written filler. Checked each sub-item mechanically against the body (lines 1-46), each grep validated against a planted positive first: (a) 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction: `grep -nE '\bNot [A-Za-z].*\. Not [A-Za-z]'` -> 0 hits (planted 'Not slow. Not fast. Right.' matched, confirming the grep works). (b) Anaphora/epistrophe triples: scanned for any word opening 3+ consecutive sentences -> max repeat count was 2 ('The'), no triple found. (c) Self-grading superlatives: `grep -niE 'one of the most|the most (useful|important|valuable)|extremely (useful|important)'` -> 0 hits. (d) Number + own retraction: `grep -niE 'could be (more|less)|roughly|approximately|about [0-9]'` -> 0 hits; the '90% agreement after three iterations' figure (line 15) is stated once, never walked back. (e) Abstraction-noun stacks: manual read of all 46 lines found no compound like 'the bounded-window reality' — nouns stay concrete (gate, judge, agent, session, model). (f) Verb triplets with an empty leg: `grep -nE '\bIt [A-Za-z]+\.\s*It [A-Za-z]+\.'` -> 0 hits. Harm absent on every sub-item.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: bold sprayed across whole lead sentences instead of marking a handle. `grep -n '\*\*' curriculum/lectures/the-gate-is-a-claim.md` over the body shows exactly 3 bold spans, one per slide, each a short naming sub-span, not a whole sentence: line 20 '**Goodhart's law**' (Gates decay slide), line 31 '**tampering**' (Change-on-recurrence slide), line 45 '**bitter lesson**' (delegation-frontier slide, the new bullet). This matches the maintainer's 2026-07-09 emphasis-pass note exactly (2 handles) plus the 2026-08-21 addition (1 more), and each slide carries ≤1 bold element -- inside budget. The new bullet's bold is a naming handle (Sutton's term), same treatment as the other two, not a lead-sentence bolding regression. Harm absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a lecture header reading as a bare label where the room needs a landed claim. All six `##` headers checked: 'Passing is not proof', 'The judge needs calibrating against your labels', 'Gates decay', 'One session is a sample', 'Change on recurrence, not on noise' are all declarative claims. 'The delegation frontier' is a catalogue entry naming its subject (parallel to the rule's own cleared examples 'Ralph', 'The numbers') -- explicitly a NOT-violation. This rule postdates the slides-judge template's blocking/non-blocking partition (added 2026-08-15/19, template's rules-9-14 paragraph stops at 14) so it is unlisted there; classifying by the template's own stated principle -- 'I cannot follow this' is blocking, 'this could be tighter' is a TODO -- a label-vs-claim header slip does not block comprehension of the slide beneath it, so I score it non-blocking (TODO), same bucket as sibling rule 6 (header self-carry). Harm absent regardless: no header in this file needed reclassifying.
